Maria: Heads up — customer 'ClipperAI' reporting intermittent 502/503s on the /v1/generate endpoint since 2026-03-15 08:10 UTC. Example request-id: req_3a98c241. They use streaming=true and long prompts (~3k tokens). Can we get a minimal repro (curl + py/js/go) and steps for a debug bundle?

Dan: Thanks — can you paste the exact curl the customer used (headers + body) and a truncated runtime log snippet? Also confirm whether they're using our hosted API or Dedicated.

Maria: Hosted API. Truncated runtime log below: 
```
2026-03-15T08:10:12Z runtime: request=req_3a98c241 status=503 err="upstream timeout" model=redwood-tiny seq=512 latency=1203ms
2026-03-15T08:10:13Z runtime: request=req_3a98c241 trace=task=decode kvcache=miss worker=worker-7
```

Maria: Here's the curl they ran (sanitized keys):
```bash
curl -i \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -H "X-Request-Id: req_3a98c241" \

  -d '{
    "model": "redwood-tiny",
    "stream": true,
    "max_tokens": 1024,

```

Alex: Nice. I made three tiny repro snippets (non-streaming and streaming variants). They use the same request-id header so our logs match. Replace REDWOOD_API_KEY and prompt.

Alex: Python (requests, streaming):
```python
import requests

url = "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate"
headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_KEY",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "X-Request-Id": "req_3a98c241"
}
json = {
    "model": "redwood-tiny",
    "stream": True,
    "max_tokens": 1024,
    "prompt": "<short prompt to repro>"
}

with requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=json, stream=True, timeout=30) as r:
    r.raise_for_status()
    for line in r.iter_lines():
        if line:
            print(line.decode())
```

Alex: Node (fetch, streaming):
```javascript
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const url = 'https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate';
const opts = {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_KEY',
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'X-Request-Id': 'req_3a98c241'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-tiny', stream: true, max_tokens: 1024, prompt: '<short prompt>' })
};
fetch(url, opts).then(res => {
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(res.statusText);
  const reader = res.body.getReader();
  return reader.read().then(function process({ done, value }) {
    if (done) return;
    process(reader.read());
  });
}).catch(console.error);
```

Alex: Go (simple POST):
```go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "io"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)
func main() {
  body := []byte(`{"model":"redwood-tiny","stream":true,"max_tokens":1024,"prompt":"<short prompt>"}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate", bytes.NewReader(body))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  req.Header.Set("X-Request-Id", "req_3a98c241")
  client := &http.Client{}
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err != nil { panic(err) }
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  io.Copy(os.Stdout, resp.Body)
  fmt.Println()
}
```

Jules: I'll collect a debug bundle from our side. For customer-side artifacts, ask them to run this helper script and upload the tar to the support ticket. It gathers request headers, curl with verbose, tcpdump for 30s, and Node/Python logs.

Jules: helper.sh:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e
OUT=clipperai-debug-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).tgz
mkdir -p /tmp/debugbundle && pushd /tmp/debugbundle >/dev/null
# capture curl run (replace values)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "X-Request-Id: req_3a98c241" -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-tiny","stream":true,"prompt":"<paste prompt>"}' > client_curl_output.txt 2>&1 || true
# tcpdump 30s (requires sudo)
sudo timeout 30 tcpdump -w tcpdump.pcap -c 1000 || true
# collect runtime logs (if customer has local logs)
cp /var/log/redwood/client.log client.log 2>/dev/null || true
# package
tar czf /tmp/$OUT . || true
echo "/tmp/$OUT"
popd >/dev/null
```
